messages:
maria: quick escalation — ACME's onprem Dedicated cluster (#dc-eu-2) is seeing streaming SSE responses abruptly cut mid-sentence. client reconnects -> sometimes they see duplicated trailing tokens (client sees end of partial sentence twice). Customer reports this happens mostly behind their corporate proxy. Repro steps they gave below. attaching ingress/nginx chunk logs and a minimal curl repro. can someone look? :frowning_face:

olivia: thanks, maria. customer says it started after a proxy config change last week (keepalive tweak). they believe proxy inserts periodic TCP keepalive packets and that might split chunks. they sent pcap & nginx access logs — forwarded to this thread.

maria: pasted the minimal repro they ran (they're using an on-prem ingress + corp proxy stack):

```
# client
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://redwood.acme.internal/v1/streams?model=xlarge"\n```

Their capture shows a single SSE event written from the server but the on-prem proxy splits the TCP payload into two packets with a flush in between. Client-side receives: first packet contains `data: {"text":"The model predicts an...` then second packet contains `continued text"}`

sam (eng-runtime): interesting. two common failure modes: 1) proxy/nginx buffering/flush behavior cutting CRLF boundaries, 2) MTU/TCP segmentation causing the language of the SSE event to split mid-json and client reconcilers to re-emit partial tokens. both can make client libs retry and re-process. can you paste a short excerpt of the raw bytes?

maria: here's a trimmed hex excerpt from their pcap (showing split after 1024 bytes):

```
... 0d0a 6461 7461 3a20 7b22 7465 7874 223a 2248 656c 6c6c 6f 2c20 776f 726c 64 0d0a 0d0a
# then second packet starts
7b22 636f 6e74 696e 7565 6422 3a20 22... 0d0a 0d0a
```

sam (eng-runtime): hmm that hex shows the second packet begins with a new `{` — looks like server may have streamed two JSON objects back to back but proxy is inserting an extra flush so the client sees an incomplete first object followed by a second object that looks like a duplicate fragment. could also be that the server writes large buffer and OS/TCP stacks segment it. two immediate asks: (A) can we get the runtime's per-request `sse-chunk-trace` for one failing request? (B) can they try `curl --http1.1 --no-buffer` to see if client-side behavior changes?

lee (eng-infra): a couple infra notes: corporate proxies often have `proxy_buffering on;` or `proxy_buffers` small values which force flushes. on nginx ingress we recommend `proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding off;` for SSE endpoints. also check `tcp_mtu_probing` and TSO/GSO offload settings on the gateway NICs — on some older Windows load balancers that causes different segmentation.

maria: customer tried toggling the keepalive interval to 30s -> they say problem frequency decreased but did not disappear. they also tested bypassing corp-proxy (direct to ingress) and problem disappeared. so strong signal it's proxy-related.

olivia: customer asked if Redwood can do anything server-side to avoid this. suggestions? they are worried about duplicate tokens causing billing + UX confusion.

sam (eng-runtime): server-side mitigations we can try:
- ensure we always emit SSE events with explicit boundaries and final `\n\n` (we already do).
- add a small per-write trailing sentinel marker like `\n:__rw_chunk_eom__\n\n` and client can ignore `:`-prefixed comments — but that requires client change which we prefer to avoid.
- more robust: implement idempotent chunk framing with event `id` increments so if client reconnects we can advise clients to resume after last seen `id` (resume semantics). that requires protocol work but avoids duplicates.

lee (eng-infra): short-term we can try to reduce the server-side write size so OS doesn't coalesce huge buffers that the proxy then splits. i can add a runtime config to cap write size to 512 bytes for a few minutes to see if frequency goes down.

maria: customer also attached ingress (nginx) error log with `upstream prematurely closed connection` entries around the same time. copying excerpt:

```
2026/02/12 14:03:11 [warn] 12345#0: *789 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.1.2.3, server: redwood, request: "GET /v1/streams?model=xlarge HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.2.3.4:8080/", host: "redwood.acme.internal"
```

sam (eng-runtime): that upstream warning could be the runtime closing idle keepalive/connections or the proxy giving up during a long-lived stream. runtime will cross-check connection lifecycle logs for the request id — can you provide request id or approximate timestamp?

maria: timestamps aligned: ~2026-02-12T14:03:10Z (attached). customer gave request-id `req-0a1b2c3d`.

sam (eng-runtime): thanks. i've kicked off `sse-chunk-trace` for `req-0a1b2c3d` — will paste when available. also, can you ask customer to try `curl -H "Cache-Control: no-transform"`? some proxies will reserialize or inject transformations unless that header is present.

deploy-bot: canary deploy finished on infra-dedicated/ingress at 2026-02-12T13:58:00Z — no restarts reported after deploy.

lee (eng-infra): ok action items I can do now:
- temporarily set runtime write cap to 512b for onprem Dedicated for this customer and monitor.
- provide a small nginx snippet for customers to set on their corp-proxy to avoid chunk-splitting:

```
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Connection "";
proxy_buffering off;
chunked_transfer_encoding off;
proxy_busy_buffers_size 256k;
```

maria: I've proposed those to customer: 1) try bypass corp-proxy -> confirms it's proxy. 2) try curl tricks (`--no-buffer`, `Cache-Control: no-transform`) 3) set above nginx config if they control proxy. they're going to try bypass tomorrow morning their time and will also capture a new pcap.

olivia: also flagged billing team — if duplicates keep happening we might temporarily suppress duplicate billing on reconnects for the customer while we triage. pinging @billing in a separate thread.

sam (eng-runtime): long-term we should spec an opt-in resume protocol for SSE (simple event IDs and resume-after semantics). filing an RFC in a follow-up issue. for now i'll watch the chunk trace and share logs.

maria: thanks all. i'll update the customer and post results from tomorrow's bypass test. keeping thread pinned. :thumbsup:
